assertions.description: The WebTransportReceiveStream interface object is exposed on the global.
WebTransportReceiveStream.prototype's direct prototype is ReadableStream.prototype, per the IDL inheritance 'WebTransportReceiveStream : ReadableStream'.
getStats is the subclass's own prototype method and is a function.
Plain ReadableStream.prototype does not gain getStats — only receive streams carry per-stream stats.
getReader is inherited from ReadableStream rather than redefined, so reading a receive stream is exactly reading a ReadableStream.
The interface has no constructor: new WebTransportReceiveStream() throws a TypeError. Instances only come from a session.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransportReceiveStream !== 'function') return false; try { new WebTransportReceiveStream(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A plain ReadableStream is not an instanceof WebTransportReceiveStream — the new type check is meaningful.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransportReceiveStream !== 'function') return false; const s = new ReadableStream(); return !(s instanceof WebTransportReceiveStream) && !('getStats' in s); })()

assertions.description: On a live incoming stream, getStats() resolves a dictionary with numeric bytesReceived and bytesRead where bytesRead <= bytesReceived. Obtaining an instance requires an established HTTP/3 session, which this static showcase cannot provide.
assertions.test: Requires a live HTTP/3 WebTransport server to deliver an incoming stream; no instance of WebTransportReceiveStream can exist here without one.

assertions.description: WebTransportReceiveStream is [Transferable]: a live instance can be posted to a worker with a transfer list. Needs a live instance, so it cannot be executed from this showcase.
assertions.test: Requires a live instance from an established session to postMessage with a transfer list.
